rationale: The market has validated willingness to pay — Originality.ai and GPTZero charge $10–$30/seat/mo — and the buyer is a nameable role (newsletter editor, community moderator, content ops manager at a small publisher) who already buys software tools. However, responsiveness is untested (default 2), the source signal is an HN feature-request thread rather than direct buyer complaints, and the space has several established competitors making defensibility low. The total of 5.9 clears the validate threshold but does not reach the 6.5 needed for build, so the next step is outreach to 10–20 newsletter editors to confirm active budget and dissatisfaction with existing tools before committing to build.
solution_plan: WHAT: A lightweight AI-content detection micro-service that accepts a URL or pasted text and returns a confidence score plus a shareable badge/label, priced at ~$19/mo per seat for newsletter editors and small platform operators. BUILD: The factory wires a Claude prompt (using Claude's own pattern-recognition on writing style, hedging language, and structural tells) to a simple landing page with an input form, a Stripe payment link for a monthly subscription, and an email delivery of the scored report — no coding by Youval. SELL: Outreach targets newsletter operators listed on public directories (Substack leaderboard, Beehiiv featured creators) and community moderators on LinkedIn; the factory drafts and queues cold emails for Youval's approval before any send. MAINTAIN: Paid subscribers submit text via a form, Claude scores it, results are emailed automatically; billing runs through Stripe; support queries are handled by a Claude-powered reply draft that Youval approves. The only recurring human touch is approving outreach batches and the occasional edge-case support reply. CAVEAT: Detection accuracy is a hard limitation — Claude is not a fine-tuned classifier and false-positive rates may frustrate buyers; this must be disclosed clearly and tested in validation before building.
notes: No build_gate failures — all four required gates (operational_autonomy 7 ≥ 7, buildability_with_ai 7 ≥ 6, buyer_clarity 6 ≥ 6, willingness_to_pay 6 ≥ 5) technically pass, but total 5.9 < 6.5 min_total_to_build caps stage at validate regardless. Key validation question: do newsletter editors find existing tools (Originality.ai, GPTZero) adequate, and is there a gap this service can credibly fill given Claude's non-specialist detection capability?
